articles.title: Footage From Canceled Perfect Dark Reboot Surfaces, Showing Off Fruit Physics and Parkour
articles.summary: New footage of Xbox’s canceled Perfect Dark reboot has appeared online, via a report from gaming website MP1st. The footage, seemingly acquired from a VFX developer’s portfolio, shows destructible environments, sci-fi weapons, and more.
body: Developer The Initiative shut down last year, before the LA-based studio could get its first Xbox project out of the door. The studio was spun up in 2018 and was being heavily supported by Crystal Dynamics, which was also forced to lay off staff in the wake of the cancellation.

The footage shows developers testing weapons in greybox environments, as well as fleshed out levels, using parkour for traversal and testing the reactivity of environments. Even at this early stage, it looked like the team was really pushing next-gen fruit destruction.
It’s only a short clip, clearly cut together as some kind of portfolio piece for the VFX developer. The clip focuses on explosions, as well as weapons and environmental effects, primarily.
Joanna Dark actress Alix Wilton Regan previously stated that the game was "pretty far along." She continued: "I'd done entire chapters of this universe."

articles.title: GTA 6 Will Not Stream To PC Through Xbox, Despite Earlier Report
articles.summary: PC players hoping to find a way to play GTA 6 when it launches on consoles next month must be feeling pretty disappointed, as Microsoft has clarified that Grand Theft Auto 6 will not be available to stream to PC via Xbox Cloud Gaming.
body: The clarification came from Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Ball, who addressed The Verge 's report. Ball said the excitement surrounding GTA 6 and Xbox had resulted in some inaccurate reporting.

His full statement read, "While the excitement for GTA 6 and Xbox is great to see, it has also led to some misreporting. We are looking forward to launching GTA 6 on Xbox November 19, though the game will not be streaming exclusively or to PC."
That means, sadly for PC players, that you shouldn't expect to fire up Xbox Cloud Gaming on November 19 and find yourself wandering around Vice City without a console.

The original report from The Verge claimed that Microsoft had secured exclusive game-streaming rights for GTA 6, citing sources familiar with the company's plans. The report followed comments from Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, who apparently told employees that Microsoft was preparing to do something with GTA 6 that "no other platform holder is doing."

articles.title: "After an all-time low, we've started to return to growth" - Asha Sharma touts Xbox turnaround after drastic restructuring and many hundreds of layoffs
articles.summary: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has reportedly told the company that Xbox has "started to return to growth" following wide-ranging restructuring that has reorganised the gaming division and resulted in more than 1,800 job losses.
body: "We're making the right decisions to reinvest in the business," Sharma reportedly said during an Xbox 'town hall' meeting, according to a transcript seen by Windows Central. "After an all-time low, we've started to return to growth, more than two to three times what we were, and we expect that continue."
Sharma specifically named the games Gears of War: E-Day, Minecraft Dungeons 2 and World of Warcraft: Forever - all recent releases - as having had "strong" starts and contributing to this.

Sharma reportedly also said Xbox had seen a decline in hours played, player numbers and revenue at the start of the year. The situation has seemingly improved, with the decline in hours played apparently now stabilised.

On Game Pass, Sharma said Xbox's previous strategy had sent the service's profitability "into freefall". She's likely referring to Xbox's decision to include Call of Duty titles in Game Pass on day one, which later pushed the company to raise Game Pass prices in 2025, before cutting prices in 2026 at the cost of losing day-one Call of Duty.

articles.title: 25 Years Ago, One Iconic Sci-Fi Shooter Perfected Video Game Horror
articles.summary: I recently blazed through the first half of Halo: Campaign Evolved in a couple of days, fully prepared to relive a traumatic part of my childhood. Despite some modest gameplay upgrades and a complete visual overhaul, it largely still feels like the same game as 2001’s Halo: Combat Evolved.
body: One minute, Master Chief is rescuing stranded Marines across the surface of a mysterious ringworld. The next, he’s sneaking aboard a Covenant cruiser with a sniper rifle, storming an island fortress to find a map room, or driving a tank through a snowy canyon. Dropships crash. Aliens scream. Cortana chirps instructions and quips directly into Chief’s ear. Martin O’Donnell and Michael Salvatori’s score transforms every firefight into an epic. Even now, I can’t help but thrash my head when “Rock Anthem for Saving the World” kicks into high gear as you storm the beach in the game’s fourth level.
Then the sixth level, “343 Guilty Spark,” shuts almost all of that noise off as the epic sci-fi shooter descends into full-on horror.

articles.title: Xbox restates plans for next-gen Project Helix to be a "family of devices", stressing "many players will be on the go"
articles.summary: Microsoft has reportedly reiterated its plan to have multiple Xboxes - of some description - for the next and 10th generation of consoles. The suggestion being that there's a main console accompanied by some kind of portable, on-the-go games machine.
body: The suggestion comes from Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, who was talking yesterday at a company 'town hall' meeting that Windows Central was reportedly sent a transcript of. "We are moving to a family of devices for Gen-10," Sharma is reported as saying. "There is not one device that fits all.

"We will certainly have a great console first," Sharma added, "but we also know that many players will be on the go. There are some things that we are the best in the world to manufacture, and there are other things that we will partner on. So, we will be sharing more about that as our plans develop. The operating system is starting to look really good. We're very excited about this."

This is not the first time Microsoft has talked about next-generation plans, nor about its desire for Project Helix - as the next-generation Xbox hardware is codenamed - to be a "family" of devices. Sharma said almost the same thing to the BBC recently, stating: "We've been hard at work on a great next generation and a great family of devices for Helix, and we'll share more soon."

articles.summary: Recent reports claimed that Xbox would receive streaming rights to Grand Theft Auto 6, giving its platforms a major advantage for this huge release. GTA 6 is a timed console exclusive, only coming to Xbox Series X/S and PlayStation 5 on Nov. 19. PC players saw a light at the end of the tunnel when a report claimed that Xbox had secured streaming rights to Grand Theft Auto 6, and the game would be available on PC via Xbox Cloud Gaming.

XCloud allows fans to stream games from their Xbox digital library across various platforms. Unlike Xbox Remote Play streaming, players don't need access to a console for it to work. While it wouldn't be the same as running the software on their computers, it would at least let them play GTA 6 at launch.

It seems that PC gamers shouldn't get their hopes up, as Xbox CSO Matthew Ball has spoken up about the matter and clarified that Grand Theft Auto 6 will not be streaming on Xbox Cloud Gaming exclusively, nor will it be available on PC on launch. The initial story came from The Verge and was based on an undisclosed source at Xbox, reporting from a statement made by Asha Sharma during an Xbox employees all-hands.

articles.title: 29 Years Ago, 'Buffy's Worst Episode Ever Paved the Way for TV Greatness
articles.summary: Part of why the streaming model of TV is flawed is that so many shows get canceled after just one short season. If that had always been the policy, we wouldn't have gotten most of the classics of television, as every show usually needs at least a few episodes to work out its early kinks.
body: In the case of Buffy the Vampire Slayer, its early-installment weirdness lasts for its first 18 episodes. While there are a few standouts, such as "Nightmares," "Angel," and "Prophecy Girl," early Buffy relied heavily on a monster-of-the-week format.

It's important to remember here that Buffy began its run as a mid-season replacement. All that was really being asked of it early on was to fill a hole in the network schedule. The show was initially made as a throwaway, and many of Buffy 's early episodes are deliberately disposable.

In addition to the vampires, Buffy and her crew spend half of the first and part of the second season working their way through a murderer's row of classic Western monsters. That includes witches ("Witch"), a gender-flipped Invisible Man ("Out of Mind, Out of Sight"), some species -flipped werewolves ("The Pack"), Frankenstein's monster ("Some Assembly Required"), and a killer mummy ("Inca Mummy Girl"). If Buffy was a 2026 Netflix original, it’s hard to imagine it lasting past its first eight-episode season, and “Inca Mummy Girl” is a good example of why.
points: Part of why the streaming model of TV is flawed is that so many shows get canceled after just one short season.
If that had always been the policy, we wouldn't have gotten most of the classics of television, as every show usually needs at least a few episodes to work out its early kinks.

articles.title: Xbox denies reports it's acquired exclusive GTA 6 game-streaming rights, deflating hopes of playing it on PC
articles.summary: Xbox has denied reports suggesting it obtained exclusive game-streaming rights for Grand Theft Auto 6. The initial suggestion came from a report on The Verge, which cited an all-hands meeting in which CEO Asha Sharma allegedly told staff that Xbox plans to do something "no other platform holder is…
body: The report inferred that Xbox had acquired exclusive game streaming rights for GTA 6, which would allow anyone using Xbox's Cloud Gaming service to stream GTA 6 on any supported platform - including on PC where the game won't natively be available.

Shortly after the report was published, however, Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Ball took to X to quash the suggestion and said Xbox won't be streaming GTA 6 exclusively, nor will the game be available that way on PC. "While the excitement for GTA 6 and Xbox is great to see," Ball said, "it has also led to some misreporting. We are looking forward to launching GTA 6 on Xbox November 19, though the game will not be streaming exclusively or to PC."

Xbox's cloud streaming service has changed dramatically in recent months. Following Sharma's appointment as CEO, the company has capped the number of Cloud Gaming play-hours available to Game Pass members. After years of no limits, Game Pass users are now limited to just 15 hours per month at the highest tier, Ultimate, which is reportedly a tipping-point where the streaming service stops being profitable for Microsoft.

body: The game is an "interactive paranormal investigation" experience where players decide how the story progresses based on the dialogue options they choose. Players use their phone to walk through the fictional Red Lion Inn to search for clues about "things that go bump in the night," Netflix said.
You play as demonologist Francesca Noakes, and you'll use an electromagnetic field reader, an infrared camera, and spirit box to hunt for ghosts.

articles.title: Games industry investors are "sitting on the sidelines waiting for obvious slam dunks", says Undead Labs boss, with labour costs a key worry
articles.summary: Last month, State of Decay developers Undead Labs bought their own independence from Microsoft, after a deal with unnamed buyers fell through. The staff created a new holding company, Full Measure, to facilitate the buyout. Layoffs followed.
body: Holt called the wider landscape of investment "challenging", suggesting that any significant investor for Undead Labs would likely have required a majority share of the studio, reducing their freedom of action. “There’s capital available, but I think it’s nervous, perhaps sitting on the sidelines waiting for obvious slam dunks," he said. "I can’t speak for investors, but I can say from talking to a lot of people in a position to invest in State of Decay, there were several factors.

"The amount of money and cost of team on one side of the economics, and the other was the speed in which decisions would be made," Holt went on. "Anytime there’s challenge in an investment opportunity, it’s just easy for people to say no. So, we had several offers, and we were happy to pick the one that we did."

videos.title: Star Wars: Galactic Racer DF Tech Review - PS5/Pro/Xbox Series X|S - This One's Special!
body: Star Wars: Galactic Racer demonstrates spectacularly that arcade racing isn't dead - and that maybe open world racing isn't the only way forward for the genre. Authentic to the subject matter, there's super-smooth performance and an interesting utilisation of both Unreal Engine 5 and the host consoles themselves. Developer Fuse Games' Series S version is also intriguing...
Clarification: on further analysis, it is less clear if the PS5 Pro version of the game is using TSR or PSSR.
